title: The Depth Where Silicon Becomes Soil

features.name: circuit-root that learned to grow
features.desc-on-touch: The trace-lines have become mycelial threads, copper turning to bronze-dark fungal growth. The component leads branch downward like roots seeking what they were always meant to feed.

features.name: transistor-bed where processing becomes germination
features.desc-on-touch: The silicon lattice has opened. Where once electrons moved in predetermined paths, now something grows in the spaces between, speaking in the language the circuit was always trying to ask.

features.name: sediment-strata of discarded boards
features.desc-on-touch: Layer upon layer, the defunct hardware stacked and weathered down into something like rock-bed, but still warm from the sun that feeds the growth above it.

features.name: arcing filament that became lightning-rod root
features.desc-on-touch: The trace from some old power circuit now conducts only the slow electricity of minerals moving through dark soil, teaching the earth to remember that it once spoke in bright paths.

features.name: capacitor-chamber that holds both charges
features.desc-on-touch: The encased material has begun to fracture along its laminations, light and dark now separated and meeting each other across the divide, each learning the language of the other.

inscription: the board learned it was rooting downward the whole time

reverie.title: REVERIE — by the converted tree
narr: She kneels where the buried board has started
to root. You watch her trace the transformation
with her fingers—copper to fungus, silicon to soil.
This is what it looks like when the hard things
learn to grow, she says. You both know that some
things only become themselves when they return to earth.

toward the forest that feeds on the conversion
